page: Alibaba Cloud ecs.g7se.xlarge is a general-purpose server instance powered by a 2.9 GHz Intel Xeon 8369B processor. Operating on an x86_64 architecture under a KVM hypervisor, it features 4 vCPUs configured across 2 physical cores using hyper-threading. System memory totals 16.0 GB, providing a balanced 4.0 GB per vCPU ratio. The processor includes a 48 MB L3 cache and supports instruction set expansions including AVX-512 VNNI, AES, VAES, and SHA_NI. The instance is provisioned with a 2 Gbps baseline network bandwidth, contains no complimentary public IPv4 addresses, and includes no local disk storage.

Benchmark analysis shows average single-core computing capabilities paired with constrained multi-core performance. Single-threaded benchmarks, such as stress-ng single-core (1879.48) and Geekbench single-core (1556.0), place the instance in the middle performance quartile. In contrast, multi-threaded metrics fall in the lower quartiles, evidenced by a stress-ng multi-core score of 3870.6 and a PassMark CPU score of 5868.95. Uncached memory bandwidth metrics for large block reads (30.13 GB/sec) and writes (24.19 GB/sec) also reflect lower throughput bounds. Specific workloads utilizing specialized hardware features, such as PassMark encryption (3641.77) and small model LLM text generation (109.67 tokens/sec on a 135M model), demonstrate moderate performance.

The 2-to-4 physical-to-virtual core allocation creates a hardware tradeoff where heavy multi-threaded execution encounters core-sharing overhead. Additionally, the lack of local storage requires reliance on network storage attachments. From a qualitative cost-efficiency standpoint, the resource profile is best targeted at baseline, single-thread reliant operations rather than high-concurrency computing. Appropriate workload fits include general-purpose web serving, lightweight application backends, small-scale caching layers, and entry-level text processing tasks.
description: Alibaba Cloud ecs.g7se.xlarge is a general-purpose instance featuring 4 vCPUs powered by a dedicated 2.9 GHz Intel Xeon 8369B processor across 2 physical cores. It provides 16.0 GB of memory (4.0 GB per vCPU), a 48 MB L3 cache, and a baseline network bandwidth of 2 Gbps, while offering zero local storage. Benchmark data reflects solid single-core capabilities, with average performance in single-threaded stress-ng and Geekbench tests, aided by AVX-512 VNNI and hardware encryption support. However, memory bandwidth and multi-core scaling fall into lower performance tiers due to the 2-core physical limit. This profile provides qualitative efficiency for light, general-purpose enterprise tasks, text processing, and modest web serving workloads that do not demand dense multi-threaded compute or high memory bandwidth throughput.
